text:
support_sarah: FYI — Customer 'Acme Corp' reporting intermittent 401s on our signed webhook callbacks since ~11:29 UTC. They say it spikes for a few mins then goes away. Logs show 'signature verification failed' and sometimes 'kid not found'. Anyone seen this?

ajay_infra: Can you paste an example log and which region? Is this Hosted API or Dedicated?

support_sarah: Hosted (us-west-2). Log snippet below (sanitized):
```
[2024-11-01T11:29:12Z] callback-signer verify FAILED customer=acme kid=oldKeyId err="kid not found"
[2024-11-01T11:29:13Z] callback-signer verify FAILED customer=acme err="signature validation failed"
[2024-11-01T11:29:15Z] callback-signer verify OK customer=acme kid=newKeyId
```

maria_sec: That pattern looks like a JWKS rotation vs cache TTL issue — key rotated -> some nodes use cached JWKS without the new kid -> kid not found until cache refresh. Any recent key rotation?

jordan_runtime: We rolled a key rotation yesterday for callback-signer at 2024-11-01T11:27:00Z. Also rolled a perf tweak that reduced jwks_cache_ttl from 5m to 60s to reduce memory/high churn. Might be a race where some validator instances didn't fetch on miss.

kevin_api: Our verifier logic currently: lookup by kid in local cache -> if not found return 401. We assumed background refresh would catch rotations. We don't fetch on miss right now to avoid thundering herd. That explains "kid not found" spikes during rotation windows.

ajay_infra: Two quick mitigations: 1) re-enable fetch-on-miss (with jitter/backoff) so a missing kid triggers a fetch from jwks endpoint; 2) increase jwks_cache_ttl back to 5m and add background refresh. Also add small leeway for exp/nbf (10s). Can we also confirm NTP health on the fleet? Clock skew can cause intermittent exp failures. :alarm_clock:

support_sarah: Customer provided repro steps: they replayed a callback with an older kid token and sometimes get 401. Sample curl they used (token redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...;kid=oldKeyId" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/callbacks/verify
# sometimes 401, sometimes 200
```

maria_sec: If the token contains an exp claim that's near the edge, clock skew + validation leeway matters. But the logs you pasted show explicit kid missing before signature attempt so JWKS staleness is primary.

jordan_runtime: I'm going to push a hotfix: fetch-on-miss + immediate background refresh for JWKS for the callback-signer service, and revert jwks_cache_ttl to 5m. Will add jittered backoff to avoid thundering herd. ETA ~25m.

kevin_api: Also recommend adding metrics + alert: jwks_fetch_errors > 1/min or 'kid not found' rate spike. Instrument a histogram for jwks refresh latency.

support_sarah: Notified customer about workaround (re-issuing tokens while we roll) and that we're reverting the TTL. They asked if we can give guidance to client devs — suggested robust retry on their side and ensure they re-request tokens if they see 401 on signed callbacks.

devops-bot: deploy callback-signer@2024-11-01T11:48:00Z - started (change: revert jwks_cache_ttl + fetch-on-miss hotfix)

jordan_runtime: Hotfix deployed to us-west-2 canaries. Observability shows kid-not-found rate down to zero on canaries. Rolling to rest of region now. Will follow up once fully rolled.

maria_sec: After roll, let's add an incident note: root cause = aggressive jwks_cache_ttl + key rotation + missing fetch-on-miss fallback. Remediation = revert TTL, enable fetch-on-miss, add leeway and add alerts. Also track any client tokens that had exp very close to rotation time.

support_sarah: Thanks — customer updated and will hold off re-issuing more tokens for now. Closing on our side once rollout completes.

devops-bot: deploy callback-signer@2024-11-01T11:58:30Z - completed (region: us-west-2)
summary: Customer reported intermittent 401s due to JWKS staleness + aggressive TTL; team reverted TTL and enabled fetch-on-miss hotfix.
